prov_p142.name: Thủy Đối
prov_p142.lore: Grassland on a fast river running down to the inland sea. Its people farm wheat and work the water mills that grind Thanh Mạch's grain for Tinh Hán Thành. A Water vein lies in the grass above the mills.

prov_p143.name: Thanh Mạch
prov_p143.lore: Rolling steppe and grassland along a river, the wheat land of Ngọc Hành. Its farmers grow the grain the mills of Thủy Đối grind. A vein by the river is said to make the wheat ripen evenly.

prov_p144.name: Châu Bạng
prov_p144.lore: A small stretch of rocky coast and low mountain on the inland sea. Its people dive for pearls in the shallows and burn shell and limestone for lime. A low humped hill shelters the village from the sea wind.

prov_p40.name: Tinh Hán
prov_p40.lore: Steppe and grassland around Tinh Hán Thành, Thiên Xu's port on the inland sea, where a river meets the shore. Farms and pasture feed the city, and the ore of Ngọc Hành goes out from its quays. A Water vein by the shore rises and falls with the tide.

prov_p82.name: Song Kiều
prov_p82.lore: Grassland, forest and mountain along the river road around Song Kiều Trấn, where the miners' ore has been weighed in public since 235. Carters, assayers and the Ôn clan's toll keepers live here. A warm spring on the grassland is where the carters rest their oxen.

prov_phat_y.name: Phất Y
prov_phat_y.lore: A high green valley among grey peaks and dry steppe, with the gorge of Vạn Trùng Hạp cutting through it. Phất Y Cốc's swordsmen live here and hire out across the heart. Their whetstones are cut from a quarry above the valley.

prov_thoi_tinh.name: Thối Tinh
prov_thoi_tinh.lore: Steep mountain flanks and a little badland along a river, around the forges of Thối Tinh Môn. Smiths, coal carriers and ore porters live on its slopes. An anvil-shaped peak rises above the forges, and the coal for them is dug below.

prov_r15_1.name: Cao Hàn Lĩnh
prov_r15_1.lore: Bare, very high mountains in the north-east of Ngọc Hành, part of the great snow massif. No one lives here. Calamine is dug in a low valley at its foot and carried to the forges.

prov_r15_10.name: Thập Giáp
prov_r15_10.lore: Steppe and desert along a river, around the valley of Thiết Bối Cốc. Its people gather the iron plates the valley's beasts shed and sell them to smiths. They herd goats on the steppe and keep clear of the herd's path.

prov_r15_11.name: Tà Dương Nguyên
prov_r15_11.lore: Dry steppe, desert and badland along a river in the west of Ngọc Hành. No village stands here. Swarms of spirit locusts rise from a ridge in late summer, and herders drive their flocks away from them.

prov_r15_12.name: Thiết Ngưu Lĩnh
prov_r15_12.lore: Mountain and steppe in the middle of Ngọc Hành, crossed by the ore roads. Its name comes from the strong oxen that haul ore over it. No one lives here but the copper crews.

prov_r15_13.name: Hỏa Diệm Lĩnh
prov_r15_13.lore: High mountain around the volcanic vent of Xích Viêm Khẩu, which Thiên Xu wards. No one may camp inside the warding ring, and no one lives here. An old fire-warden fort stands empty below the pillars.

prov_r15_14.name: Lưu Sa Nguyên
prov_r15_14.lore: Desert, steppe and high plain along a river on the western edge. Its dunes move with every storm, and no one lives here. A warm spring in the sand is the only sure water.

prov_r15_15.name: Hãn Hải Nguyên
prov_r15_15.lore: Desert and steppe along a river in the south-west. No one lives here now. A Fire and Earth vein lies on the steppe, and the cells of an ascetic sect stand empty in the mountain above.

prov_r15_16.name: Thương Mạc Nguyên
prov_r15_16.lore: Grey desert, steppe and mountain along a river in the south-west. Sand pythons hunt its dunes, and no one lives here. The empty temple of Thanh Đăng Tự stands on a mountain shoulder above the sand.

prov_r15_17.name: Vạn Nhận Lĩnh
prov_r15_17.lore: High mountains rising steeply out of the desert edge. No one lives here but a few black-silver miners. Its leaning peak is a landmark across the desert.

prov_r15_18.name: Cổ Đạo Lĩnh
prov_r15_18.lore: High mountains crossed by the oldest ore road in Ngọc Hành. Platinum is dug in its rock. On the road stands the stockade the miners' bosses held before Thiên Xu's fair weights came in 235.

prov_r15_19.name: Bát Diện Lĩnh
prov_r15_19.lore: Bare high mountains whose peaks face every direction. No one lives here. Pyrite is dug on its flanks and sold for fire-strikers and sulphur.

prov_r15_2.name: Lâm Uyên Lĩnh
prov_r15_2.lore: Very high mountains dropping to the inland sea in sheer walls, part of the great snow massif of the north-east. No one lives here. Fishermen see its cloud-hung peak from far out on the water.

prov_r15_20.name: Tiêu Thổ Lĩnh
prov_r15_20.lore: High mountains with a few small volcanic vents, running down to the coast. No one lives here; its rock is burned black in places. An old sea patrol fort stands empty on the coast below.

prov_r15_21.name: Đà Đội
prov_r15_21.lore: Steppe and mountain on the south-western edge, on the caravan road to the desert. Its people keep camels and hire them to the caravans. Great eagles nest on the cliffs above and take lambs.

prov_r15_22.name: Toái Thạch Lĩnh
prov_r15_22.lore: Mountain, desert and steppe in the south-west, its slopes covered in broken stone. Rock salt is dug here and carried to the mining villages. An old grain stockade stands empty on the high plain.

prov_r15_23.name: Bình Sa Nguyên
prov_r15_23.lore: Flat desert and steppe along a river in the south-west. No village stands here. Caravans water their horses at a warm spring on the high ground.

prov_r15_24.name: Lam Vụ Lĩnh
prov_r15_24.lore: High mountains around Thanh Ải Phong, whose haze never lifts, running down to the coast. No sect holds the peak. Jade is cut on a lower shoulder, and pilgrims have crowded its paths since the haze lifted in 1180.

prov_r15_25.name: Hùng Quan Lĩnh
prov_r15_25.lore: High bare mountains with a single pass between the western and eastern ore valleys. No one lives here. Ore trains cross the pass in summer.

prov_r15_26.name: Ngân Chu Lĩnh
prov_r15_26.lore: High mountains and forest on the coast, home to the sword-ore mine of Can Tương and the silver mine of Bạch Ngân. Miners live in the adits' camps, and Phượng Minh's border lies beyond the ridge. A boundary-stone peak stands over the mines, and an old silver fort lies on the shore.

prov_r15_27.name: Bích Thảo Lĩnh
prov_r15_27.lore: Mountain, steppe and grassland in the south-west. Herders summer their flocks on its grassy tops. No village stands here.

prov_r15_28.name: Kim Phong Lĩnh
prov_r15_28.lore: Mountain and steppe in the south-west, swept by a cold dry wind from the desert each autumn. No one lives here. Its white stone peak is seen from the caravan road.

prov_r15_29.name: Bạch Lãng Lĩnh
prov_r15_29.lore: High mountains along a river where it reaches the coast. No village stands here. Its sail-watching peak looks over the water.

prov_r15_3.name: Đông Cực Nhai
prov_r15_3.lore: Steep mountains above the eastern coast, home to the star-iron mine of Thiên Ngoại Khoáng. No one lives here but Thối Tinh Môn's miners. Below its black hawk peak opens the mouth of the deep cave Cửu U Động, which the miners do not enter.

prov_r15_30.name: Thanh Trúc Lĩnh
prov_r15_30.lore: Mountain with forest and bamboo on its southern flanks. No one lives here. Black magnetite sand is dug in a gully.

prov_r15_31.name: Hoàng Hoa
prov_r15_31.lore: Grassland and mountain in the south-east of Ngọc Hành, not far from Phượng Minh's border. Its people grow daylilies and graze cattle. A Wood vein lies in the grass above the village.

prov_r15_32.name: Ngọa Vân Nguyên
prov_r15_32.lore: Mountain, grassland and badland on the southern coast. Cloud lies on its grassy plateau most mornings. No one lives here.

prov_r15_33.name: Mục Khuyển
prov_r15_33.lore: Grassland, steppe, badland and mountain in the south-west. Its herders keep sheep and breed sheepdogs for all of Ngọc Hành. Garnets are dug in the mountain, and an Earth vein lies on the high plain.

prov_r15_34.name: Phi Bộc Lĩnh
prov_r15_34.lore: High mountains with bamboo and forest along a river that falls in long cascades. No one lives here. Silver is dug in thin veins in its rock.

prov_r15_35.name: Trùng Loan Lĩnh
prov_r15_35.lore: High mountains standing in rank behind rank in the south of Ngọc Hành. No one lives here. Banded marble is quarried on a low shoulder.

prov_r15_36.name: Lục Thủy Câu
prov_r15_36.lore: Mountain, grassland and steppe along a green river in the south. Herders summer here, and a copper mine works the gully. No village stands here.

prov_r15_37.name: Chu Nhai Câu
prov_r15_37.lore: Red badland, mountain and grassland along a river in the south. No one lives here. Copper ore is dug from the red cliffs by the river.

prov_r15_38.name: Bích Tiêu Lĩnh
prov_r15_38.lore: High mountains with forest and bamboo in the south. No one lives here. An old boundary stockade lies under an avalanche slope.

prov_r15_39.name: Song Tuyền Lĩnh
prov_r15_39.lore: High mountains along a river in the south, fed by two springs from the same rock. No one lives here. Topaz is dug in its rock.

prov_r15_4.name: Thanh Ngạn Lĩnh
prov_r15_4.lore: Mountain and forest running down to the inland sea in the north-east. No one lives here. Its hibiscus peak flowers in pink every summer.

prov_r15_40.name: Thiên Biên Lĩnh
prov_r15_40.gloss: Ridge at the Edge of the Sky
prov_r15_40.lore: High mountains on the southern rim of Ngọc Hành, looking down toward Thính Vũ's vein of Kinh Lôi Mạch. No one lives here. An old border watch fort stands on its heights.

prov_r15_41.name: Lan Khê Lĩnh
prov_r15_41.lore: Mountain and forest along an orchid-lined brook in the south. No one lives here. A red silver mine and an old toll stockade lie on the old ore road.

prov_r15_42.name: Thiên Lý Lĩnh
prov_r15_42.lore: High mountains around Cùng Mục Phong, the Peak of the Farthest Sight. Phất Y Cốc's disciples climb through it to read the sword cuts of 1130. An old bandit stockade stands empty on its heights.

prov_r15_43.name: Bích Lưu Lĩnh
prov_r15_43.lore: High mountains and a little bamboo along a green torrent in the south. No one lives here. Gold is washed from the torrent's gravel.

prov_r15_5.name: Huyền Nham Nhai
prov_r15_5.lore: Mountain cliffs above the eastern coast, home to the deep black iron shaft of Huyền Thiết Khoáng. Miners and oxen live in the mine's camp. A massive peak stands over the winch house.

prov_r15_6.name: Thằng Ma
prov_r15_6.lore: Grassland, forest and steppe in the north of Ngọc Hành. Its people grow hemp and twist it into rope for the mines' winches and hoists. A Wood vein lies in the forest above.

prov_r15_7.name: Khô Thảo Nguyên
prov_r15_7.lore: Grassland and badland in the north-west, dry by midsummer. No one lives here. Orpiment is dug here, and a red Earth and Fire vein lies in the badland.

prov_r15_8.name: Mã Đầu
prov_r15_8.lore: Steppe, badland and grassland along a river in the north-west. Its people load ore and wool onto river boats at the landing. Wild spirit bulls graze the steppe, and an old sect stands empty on the grassland.

prov_r15_9.name: Hải Giác Lĩnh
prov_r15_9.lore: Mountain and forest on a cape of the inland sea. No one lives here. Blue iron is dug on its slopes, and fishermen steer by its peak.

prov_p142_spirit_vein_1.name: Thanh Lưu Mạch
prov_p142_spirit_vein_1.look: A spring in the grass above the mills, so clear that its pebbles seem to float.
prov_p142_spirit_vein_1.lore: A small vein (linh mạch) whose qi (linh khí) runs to Water. The millers say their wheels turn smoother on the stream it feeds, and they never let cattle drink at its head.

prov_p143_spirit_vein_1.name: Kim Tuệ Mạch
prov_p143_spirit_vein_1.look: A riverside field where the wheat always ripens first and stands tallest.
prov_p143_spirit_vein_1.lore: Its qi runs to Earth and Wood. The village threshes the first sheaf from it before any other, and seed from this field is traded for twice its weight in common grain.

prov_p144_peak_1.name: Quy Bối Sơn
prov_p144_peak_1.look: A low, humped hill of grey rock on the shore, shaped like a turtle's back, its seaward side white with spray.
prov_p144_peak_1.lore: It shelters Châu Bạng from the sea wind. Its qi runs to Water, calm and slow, and divers sit on its crown before the season to steady their breath.

prov_p144_mine_2.name: Thạch Hôi Khoáng
prov_p144_mine_2.look: A white limestone quarry by the sea, with kilns burning shell and stone into lime.
prov_p144_mine_2.lore: Its lime makes the mortar of Tinh Hán's walls and the packing between the ribs of the bone reef. The burners' eyes are always red, and they wash them in sea water each evening.

prov_p40_spirit_vein_1.name: Triều Tịch Mạch
prov_p40_spirit_vein_1.look: A pool in the steppe near the shore that rises and falls with the tide, though it does not touch the sea.
prov_p40_spirit_vein_1.lore: Its qi runs to Water. Tinh Hán's formation masters know of it but have never drawn on it, saying a vein that keeps the sea's time will not keep a city's.

prov_p82_hot_spring_1.name: Xuân Thủy Thang
prov_p82_hot_spring_1.look: A warm, shallow spring in the grassland with stone troughs where oxen stand.
prov_p82_hot_spring_1.lore: Carters rest their oxen here after the ore road. The Ôn clan charges nothing for it, which surprises everyone who knows the clan.

prov_p82_minor_seat_p.name: Chân Kim Các
prov_p82_minor_seat_p.look: A two-storey stone pavilion in a forest clearing, its yard full of crucibles and its doors bound in bronze.
prov_p82_minor_seat_p.lore: Assayers and refiners of spirit ore founded this pavilion in 980 beside Song Kiều's open scales, sworn to Thiên Xu. They test and refine ore for the mines of Ngọc Hành, and their stamp on an ingot is taken at Thiên Quyền Thị without a second weighing.

prov_phat_y_mine_1.name: Lệ Thạch Khoáng
prov_phat_y_mine_1.look: A grey quarry of fine sandstone high on the mountain, its slabs split and stacked by the path to the valley.
prov_phat_y_mine_1.lore: Phất Y Cốc's whetstones are cut here. Every disciple cuts and dresses his own first stone, and carries it until it is worn through.

prov_thoi_tinh_peak_1.name: Thiết Châm Phong
prov_thoi_tinh_peak_1.look: A flat-topped peak of dark rock above the forges, shaped like an anvil and often ringed with forge smoke.
prov_thoi_tinh_peak_1.lore: Thối Tinh Môn's smiths say the sky hammers stars on it. Its qi runs to Metal, hard and ringing, and smiths sit on its flat top to temper their own bodies before forging a great blade.

prov_thoi_tinh_mine_2.name: Thạch Thán Khoáng
prov_thoi_tinh_mine_2.look: A black adit below the forges, with coal baskets carried up a stair cut in the slope.
prov_thoi_tinh_mine_2.lore: Its hard black coal feeds Thối Tinh Môn's forges. The porters climb the stair a hundred times a day and are paid by the basket.

prov_r15_1_peak_1.name: Ngân Giáp Phong
prov_r15_1_peak_1.look: A great snow peak of the north-eastern massif, its snowfields plated in overlapping scales like armour.
prov_r15_1_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water, cold enough to bite through robes. No one has climbed it; cultivators who meditate on its lower snowfields say it hardens the body like quenched steel.

prov_r15_1_mine_2.name: Lô Cam Khoáng
prov_r15_1_mine_2.look: Pale, crumbly ore pits in a low valley at the mountain's foot, with ore spread to roast on stone hearths.
prov_r15_1_mine_2.lore: Calamine from here is carried to Thối Tinh Môn and alloyed with copper into brass for fittings and array rings. The roasting fumes turn the valley's grass white.

prov_r15_10_village_1.name: Thập Giáp Thôn
prov_r15_10_village_1.look: A river village of stone houses with iron-grey beast plates stacked against the walls.
prov_r15_10_village_1.lore: Its people gather the plates the beasts of Thiết Bối Cốc shed and sell them to smiths. They herd goats and keep out of the herd's path.

prov_r15_11_beast_lair_1.name: Phi Hoàng Cương
prov_r15_11_beast_lair_1.look: A dry steppe ridge stripped bare of grass, the ground pocked with egg holes.
prov_r15_11_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit locusts hatch here and rise in swarms in late summer. Their swarms strip fields bare, and their wings are used in talismans.

prov_r15_12_peak_1.name: Đồng Trụ Phong
prov_r15_12_peak_1.look: A tall bronze-brown pillar of rock above the ore roads, its flanks streaked green where copper weathers out.
prov_r15_12_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Ore drivers touch its foot for luck, and cultivators of Metal arts climb its pillar to feel the ore singing in the rock.

prov_r15_12_mine_2.name: Lục Đồng Khoáng
prov_r15_12_mine_2.look: Green-stained rock in a mountain cut, with a broken ore cart left on the overgrown road below.
prov_r15_12_mine_2.lore: Its green copper ore was once hauled by ox over the ridge and weighed at Song Kiều like all the ore of Ngọc Hành, until richer cuts nearer the scales took its trade.

prov_r15_13_ruin_1.name: Thủ Hỏa Bảo
prov_r15_13_ruin_1.look: A squat stone fort below the warding pillars, its walls glazed by heat.
prov_r15_13_ruin_1.lore: From 460 a garrison kept watch on the vent here. When the warding pillars were raised in 1040 the Pivot withdrew the garrison, and the fort was left.

prov_r15_14_hot_spring_1.name: Sa Nhãn Tuyền
prov_r15_14_hot_spring_1.look: A small warm pool among dunes, its water bubbling up through clean sand.
prov_r15_14_hot_spring_1.lore: It is the only sure water on the shifting plain. Travellers mark it with a tall pole so the dunes do not hide it, and replace the pole when it falls.

prov_r15_15_spirit_vein_1.name: Liệt Nhật Mạch
prov_r15_15_spirit_vein_1.look: A patch of steppe where the ground is hot even at night and the grass is scorched yellow.
prov_r15_15_spirit_vein_1.lore: Its qi runs to Fire and Earth. Fire cultivators sit here at noon, and the ascetics of the mountain above once walked here barefoot as a trial.

prov_r15_15_ruin_2.name: Khổ Tu Viện
prov_r15_15_ruin_2.look: Bare stone cells cut into a mountainside above the desert, each just big enough to sit in.
prov_r15_15_ruin_2.lore: Ascetics who fasted in the desert founded it in 610. Fewer and fewer came to take up the hard life, and by 880 the cells were empty.

prov_r15_16_beast_lair_1.name: Hôi Mãng Cương
prov_r15_16_beast_lair_1.look: A ridge of grey dunes marked with long, smooth, curving tracks.
prov_r15_16_beast_lair_1.lore: Grey spirit pythons as long as boats bury themselves here and take camels. Their skins are prized for drums, and the caravans pay well for them.

prov_r15_16_ruin_2.name: Thanh Đăng Tự
prov_r15_16_ruin_2.look: A small temple on a mountain shoulder, its roof gone and a bronze lamp still hanging in the hall.
prov_r15_16_ruin_2.lore: A small sect of monks who kept a lamp burning for travellers founded it in 450. Its last abbot died in 760 with no disciple, and the lamp went out.

prov_r15_17_peak_1.name: Ỷ Thiên Phong
prov_r15_17_peak_1.look: A tall peak leaning over the desert edge, as if propping up the sky.
prov_r15_17_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Caravans steer by it across the desert, and sword cultivators climb its overhang to practise against the wind.

prov_r15_17_mine_2.name: Ô Ngân Khoáng
prov_r15_17_mine_2.look: A narrow adit in dark mountain rock, its spoil black and heavy.
prov_r15_17_mine_2.lore: Its black silver ore, silver darkened with sulphur, is refined at Song Kiều. The crews come up the desert edge in spring and leave before the autumn wind.

prov_r15_18_peak_1.name: Thiên Môn Phong
prov_r15_18_peak_1.look: Two high summits with a deep gap between them, where the old ore road passes.
prov_r15_18_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Ore drivers call the gap the gate of heaven, and cultivators sit in it at dawn, when the wind through the gate is said to clear the meridians.

prov_r15_18_mine_2.name: Bạch Kim Khoáng
prov_r15_18_mine_2.look: A small mine high on the mountain, with heavy grey grains washed in a cold stream.
prov_r15_18_mine_2.lore: Its rare white metal does not rust or melt in a common forge. It goes straight to the Pivot's own forges for array anchors.

prov_r15_18_ruin_3.name: Thiết Môn Bảo
prov_r15_18_ruin_3.look: A stone stockade across the old ore road, its iron gate rusted open.
prov_r15_18_ruin_3.lore: The miners' bosses held this stockade from 140 to tax the ore at the gate. When Thiên Xu's assayers began to weigh ore in public at Song Kiều in 235, the miners stopped coming, and it was left.

prov_r15_19_peak_1.name: Thạch Kính Phong
prov_r15_19_peak_1.look: A peak with a smooth, polished rock face that flashes in the sun.
prov_r15_19_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Miners use its flash to signal across the valleys, and cultivators gaze into its face to calm the mind before a breakthrough.

prov_r15_19_mine_2.name: Hoàng Thiết Khoáng
prov_r15_19_mine_2.look: Brassy cubes of pyrite glittering in an abandoned grey mountain cut.
prov_r15_19_mine_2.lore: No one works it now: its pyrite fetched too little as fire-strikers or roasted sulphur. Passing travellers still fill their pockets with it, thinking it gold.

prov_r15_2_peak_1.name: Quải Vân Phong
prov_r15_2_peak_1.look: A great snow peak above the sea cliffs, clouds hanging from its shoulders like banners.
prov_r15_2_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Fishermen see it from far out on the inland sea, and cultivators of Water arts sit on its lower cliffs to draw on the sea mist.

prov_r15_20_peak_1.name: Huân Yên Phong
prov_r15_20_peak_1.look: A high peak streaked black by the smoke of small vents on its flanks.
prov_r15_20_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Fire. The ground near its vents is warm all winter, and Fire cultivators camp beside them to temper their spirit fire.

prov_r15_20_ruin_2.name: Tuần Hải Bảo
prov_r15_20_ruin_2.look: A stone fort on a coastal headland, its seaward wall cracked and its beacon cold.
prov_r15_20_ruin_2.lore: Thiên Xu built it in 650 to watch for the pirates of Thôn Hải Môn. After the Pirate Purge destroyed them in 781 the fort was not needed, and it was stood down in 790.

prov_r15_21_village_1.name: Đà Đội Thôn
prov_r15_21_village_1.look: A steppe village of stone houses with camels kneeling in the yards and bells hanging from the eaves.
prov_r15_21_village_1.lore: Its people keep camels and hire them to the desert caravans. Each camel's bell has its own note, and the owners know them in the dark.

prov_r15_21_beast_lair_2.name: Hùng Điêu Nhai
prov_r15_21_beast_lair_2.look: High cliffs above the steppe, streaked white below the nests of great golden eagles.
prov_r15_21_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit eagles nest here and take lambs and young camels. Their feathers are prized by fletchers, and Đà Đội's children are taught to lie flat when a shadow passes.

prov_r15_22_peak_1.name: Lạc Đà Phong
prov_r15_22_peak_1.look: A two-humped peak above the steppe, brown and bare.
prov_r15_22_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, slow and enduring. Caravans know they are near Đà Đội when they see it, and Earth cultivators sit in the saddle between its humps.

prov_r15_22_mine_2.name: Nham Diêm Khoáng
prov_r15_22_mine_2.look: A pink-white salt cut in the mountain, with salt blocks stacked for the mule trains.
prov_r15_22_mine_2.lore: Its rock salt goes to the mining villages of Ngọc Hành. A block of it is given to every new miner's family.

prov_r15_22_ruin_3.name: Tích Lương Trại
prov_r15_22_ruin_3.look: Stone granaries inside a broken palisade on the high plain.
prov_r15_22_ruin_3.lore: It stored grain for the miners from 300. When the grain road moved to Song Kiều in 640 the stockade was left.

prov_r15_23_hot_spring_1.name: Mã Ẩm Tuyền
prov_r15_23_hot_spring_1.look: A warm spring on the high ground above the sand, its rim trampled by hooves.
prov_r15_23_hot_spring_1.lore: Caravans water their horses here. It is said a horse that drinks here will not tire for a day.

prov_r15_24_mine_1.name: Ải Ngọc Khoáng
prov_r15_24_mine_1.look: A cut on a lower shoulder of the mountain, just below the haze line, where a soft blue-grey jade shows in the abandoned face.
prov_r15_24_mine_1.lore: The jade from here has the colour of Thanh Ải's haze. The miners never climbed above the haze line, and on the day the haze lifted in 1180 they left the cut and did not come back.

prov_r15_25_peak_1.name: Hành Vân Phong
prov_r15_25_peak_1.look: A high bare peak with clouds always drifting across its summit.
prov_r15_25_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Ore trains cross the pass below it in summer, and cultivators climb above the clouds to sit in the clear air.

prov_r15_26_peak_1.name: Giới Bi Phong
prov_r15_26_peak_1.look: A high peak with a stone stele on its summit facing the east.
prov_r15_26_peak_1.lore: Thiên Xu's boundary with Phượng Minh is marked on its summit. Its qi runs to Metal and Fire, and on clear nights the glow of the cinnabar ridge can be seen from it.

prov_r15_26_ruin_2.name: Ngân Thuyền Bảo
prov_r15_26_ruin_2.look: A stone fort on the shore, its harbour silted up into a reed marsh.
prov_r15_26_ruin_2.lore: It guarded silver shipped by sea from 460. Its harbour silted up, and by 1003 the silver went overland to Song Kiều and the fort was left.

prov_r15_27_peak_1.name: Mục Đồng Phong
prov_r15_27_peak_1.look: A grassy peak with herders' stone shelters on its top.
prov_r15_27_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Wood, mild and green. Herd boys play pipes on its summit in summer, and young cultivators find it a gentle place to first open their meridians.

prov_r15_28_peak_1.name: Bạch Thạch Phong
prov_r15_28_peak_1.look: A peak of white stone above the steppe, bright against the autumn sky.
prov_r15_28_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. It can be seen from the caravan road, and cultivators climb it in autumn when the dry wind sharpens its qi.

prov_r15_29_peak_1.name: Vọng Phàm Phong
prov_r15_29_peak_1.look: A high peak above the river mouth, looking far over the water.
prov_r15_29_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Families of sailors climb it to watch for returning sails, and leave a stone on the cairn for each one.

prov_r15_3_peak_1.name: Hắc Ưng Phong
prov_r15_3_peak_1.look: A dark peak above the eastern coast, black hawks wheeling around its summit.
prov_r15_3_peak_1.lore: Below it opens the mouth of Cửu U Động, which Thối Tinh's miners do not enter. Its qi runs to Metal, and the hawks are said to hunt only those who sleep on its summit.

prov_r15_30_peak_1.name: Quân Tử Phong
prov_r15_30_peak_1.look: A peak with bamboo on its flanks and a straight, upright rock summit.
prov_r15_30_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Scholars come to paint its bamboo, and cultivators sit among the stems to practise stillness.

prov_r15_30_mine_2.name: Hắc Sa Khoáng
prov_r15_30_mine_2.look: Black magnetite sand washed in a gully and heaped on mats, clinging to any iron tool laid on it.
prov_r15_30_mine_2.lore: Its magnetite sand is smelted into iron for tools. The washers pull it from the gravel with lodestones on strings.

prov_r15_31_village_1.name: Hoàng Hoa Thôn
prov_r15_31_village_1.look: A grassland village among fields of yellow daylilies, with cattle on the slopes.
prov_r15_31_village_1.lore: Its people grow daylilies for food and medicine and graze cattle. Dried flowers from here are sold in Tinh Hán as far as the quays.

prov_r15_31_spirit_vein_2.name: Lục Nhung Mạch
prov_r15_31_spirit_vein_2.look: A grassy slope covered in soft green moss like velvet.
prov_r15_31_spirit_vein_2.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Cattle grazed here give rich milk, and the village keeps it for the calving cows.

prov_r15_32_peak_1.name: Cô Tháp Phong
prov_r15_32_peak_1.look: A tower-like peak standing alone above the grassy plateau.
prov_r15_32_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Earth. Cloud lies around its foot most mornings, and Earth cultivators sit on its top above the cloud.

prov_r15_33_village_1.name: Mục Khuyển Thôn
prov_r15_33_village_1.look: A steppe village with sheepdogs lying at every door and flocks on the hills.
prov_r15_33_village_1.lore: Its herders breed sheepdogs for all of Ngọc Hành. A pup from here is paid for in silver.

prov_r15_33_spirit_vein_2.name: Thạch Căn Mạch
prov_r15_33_spirit_vein_2.look: A rock outcrop on the high plain, its grey stone veined like roots.
prov_r15_33_spirit_vein_2.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, deep and steady. Herders say no storm has ever knocked down a cairn built on it.

prov_r15_33_mine_3.name: Lựu Thạch Khoáng
prov_r15_33_mine_3.look: Dark red garnets in grey mountain rock, picked out by hand.
prov_r15_33_mine_3.lore: Its garnets are cut into beads, and the small ones are crushed into polishing grit for the forges of Thối Tinh.

prov_r15_34_peak_1.name: Ngọc Lâu Phong
prov_r15_34_peak_1.look: A tall pale peak above the falls, its walls stacked like the floors of a tower.
prov_r15_34_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Cultivators sit behind the falls at its foot to temper the body under the water's weight.

prov_r15_34_mine_2.name: Ngân Ti Khoáng
prov_r15_34_mine_2.look: Thin threads of native silver in a damp mountain face beside the falls.
prov_r15_34_mine_2.lore: Its silver is picked out by hand with fine chisels and refined at Song Kiều. Silversmiths value the threads for wire.

prov_r15_35_peak_1.name: Hồng Nhạn Phong
prov_r15_35_peak_1.look: A high peak where wild geese rest on its ledges on their migration.
prov_r15_35_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Hunters do not shoot the geese here, and cultivators read the seasons by their coming and going.

prov_r15_35_mine_2.name: Cẩm Thạch Khoáng
prov_r15_35_mine_2.look: A quarry of banded marble on a low shoulder, its blocks patterned like woven silk.
prov_r15_35_mine_2.lore: Its marble is carved into tables and screens for the halls of Tinh Hán. Blocks are lowered down the slope on ropes from Thằng Ma.

prov_r15_36_peak_1.name: Thanh Loa Phong
prov_r15_36_peak_1.look: A spiral-ridged green peak above the river, like a conch shell.
prov_r15_36_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herders summer below it, and cultivators climb its spiral path in one breath as a test.

prov_r15_36_mine_2.name: Đồng Tỉnh Khoáng
prov_r15_36_mine_2.look: A deep copper shaft in the gully with a windlass and leather buckets.
prov_r15_36_mine_2.lore: Its copper ore comes up by bucket and is weighed at Song Kiều. The shaft floods every spring and must be bailed by hand.

prov_r15_37_peak_1.name: Xích Dực Phong
prov_r15_37_peak_1.look: A red peak above the badland gully, its two ridges spread like wings.
prov_r15_37_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Fire with a base of Earth. Fire cultivators sit between its wings at sunset, when the red rock glows.

prov_r15_37_mine_2.name: Lam Lục Khoáng
prov_r15_37_mine_2.look: Red cliffs by the river streaked green and blue with copper ore.
prov_r15_37_mine_2.lore: Its copper ore is broken from the cliffs and floated by river to the landing at Mã Đầu.

prov_r15_38_peak_1.name: Cửu Tiêu Phong
prov_r15_38_peak_1.look: A very high peak above the forest, its summit often lost in sky.
prov_r15_38_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal, thin and sharp. Cultivators who reach its summit say the air there makes the spirit feel weightless.

prov_r15_38_ruin_2.name: Thủ Bi Trại
prov_r15_38_ruin_2.look: Broken walls under an avalanche slope, half buried in rock.
prov_r15_38_ruin_2.lore: From 520 a garrison guarded a boundary stele set after the Compact. An avalanche buried the stockade in 1006, and the stele was moved lower.

prov_r15_39_peak_1.name: Tử Cái Phong
prov_r15_39_peak_1.look: A peak with a cap of purple rock over the twin springs.
prov_r15_39_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Herb gatherers find a purple lichen on its cap that alchemists buy for calming pills.

prov_r15_39_mine_2.name: Hoàng Ngọc Khoáng
prov_r15_39_mine_2.look: Golden crystals in grey mountain rock above the river, in a cut half full of spring water.
prov_r15_39_mine_2.lore: Topaz from here was once cut at Tinh Hán into ring stones and seals, but the springs have not run low in the dry months for years, and the crews no longer come.

prov_r15_4_peak_1.name: Phù Dung Phong
prov_r15_4_peak_1.look: A forested peak above the shore that flowers pink each summer.
prov_r15_4_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Sailors on the inland sea say summer has come when its slopes turn pink.

prov_r15_40_peak_1.name: Tuyệt Bích Phong
prov_r15_40_peak_1.look: A sheer high peak on the southern rim, its walls dropping toward the south.
prov_r15_40_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. From its edge the Pivot's old watchmen could see as far as Kinh Lôi Mạch, and climbers still use their iron pegs.

prov_r15_40_mine_2.name: Tử Ngọc Khoáng
prov_r15_40_mine_2.look: A high cut showing veins of purple stone under the sheer wall.
prov_r15_40_mine_2.lore: Its purple jade is rare and goes to the Pivot for seals. The crews work only in high summer.

prov_r15_40_ruin_3.name: Nam Vọng Bảo
prov_r15_40_ruin_3.look: A stone fort on the heights, its walls broken and its watch platform facing south.
prov_r15_40_ruin_3.lore: The Pivot's border watch on the south ridge from 512, looking down toward Kinh Lôi Mạch. It was stood down in 806 after the truce.

prov_r15_41_peak_1.name: Ưng Sào Phong
prov_r15_41_peak_1.look: A peak with hawks' nests on its cliffs above the orchid brook.
prov_r15_41_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Young cultivators climb its cliffs for hawk chicks to tame.

prov_r15_41_mine_2.name: Xích Ngân Khoáng
prov_r15_41_mine_2.look: Dark red silver ore glinting in a mountain cut by the old road.
prov_r15_41_mine_2.lore: Its red silver ore is roasted on site and refined at Song Kiều. It is richer in silver than any other mine on the old road.

prov_r15_41_ruin_3.name: Hạp Khẩu Trại
prov_r15_41_ruin_3.look: A stockade half buried under a landslide at the mouth of a gorge.
prov_r15_41_ruin_3.lore: A toll stockade on the ore road from 300. A landslide buried it in 718, and the road was moved to the other bank.

prov_r15_42_ruin_1.name: Hắc Phong Trại
prov_r15_42_ruin_1.look: A stockade of rough stone on the windy heights, its walls broken.
prov_r15_42_ruin_1.lore: A bandit hold of rogue cultivators (tán tu) from 880, who robbed the ore trains. Thiên Xu cleared it in 940.

prov_r15_43_peak_1.name: Ngọc Nữ Phong
prov_r15_43_peak_1.look: A slender pale peak above the torrent, like a standing woman.
prov_r15_43_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Women cultivators of Water arts come to meditate at its foot by the torrent.

prov_r15_43_mine_2.name: Lưu Kim Khoáng
prov_r15_43_mine_2.look: Wooden sluices in the green torrent, with washers in leather aprons.
prov_r15_43_mine_2.lore: Gold is washed from the torrent's gravel after the spring floods. Every washer pays a tenth to the Pivot by weight.

prov_r15_5_peak_1.name: Trấn Sơn Phong
prov_r15_5_peak_1.look: A massive dark peak above the winch house of Huyền Thiết.
prov_r15_5_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Earth and Metal, heavy as the iron below it. Body cultivators carry stones up it to temper their bones.

prov_r15_6_village_1.name: Thằng Ma Thôn
prov_r15_6_village_1.look: A grassland village among hemp fields, with long rope walks along the lane.
prov_r15_6_village_1.lore: Its people twist hemp into rope for the mines' winches. A rope that breaks is traced back to its maker.

prov_r15_6_spirit_vein_2.name: Lục Ấm Mạch
prov_r15_6_spirit_vein_2.look: A shady forest grove above the hemp fields where the air is always cool.
prov_r15_6_spirit_vein_2.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Hemp seed soaked in its spring is said to grow the strongest fibre.

prov_r15_7_spirit_vein_1.name: Xích Long Mạch
prov_r15_7_spirit_vein_1.look: A red badland ridge winding like a dragon, warm to the touch.
prov_r15_7_spirit_vein_1.lore: Its qi runs to Earth and Fire. No grass grows on its spine, and herders say it shifts a little each century.

prov_r15_7_mine_2.name: Thư Hoàng Khoáng
prov_r15_7_mine_2.look: Bright yellow orpiment in grey mountain rock.
prov_r15_7_mine_2.lore: Its yellow pigment is sold to talisman makers and painters. It is poisonous, and the diggers wear cloth over their faces.

prov_r15_8_village_1.name: Mã Đầu Thôn
prov_r15_8_village_1.look: A river village with boats tied at a long timber landing.
prov_r15_8_village_1.lore: Its people load ore and wool onto river boats bound for the coast. They are paid by the load and counted by a tally stick.

prov_r15_8_beast_lair_2.name: Hắc Ngưu Cương
prov_r15_8_beast_lair_2.look: A steppe ridge trampled by a herd of black bulls.
prov_r15_8_beast_lair_2.lore: Wild spirit bulls graze here and charge anything that comes near. Their horns are carved into bows.

prov_r15_8_ruin_3.name: Hoành Đao Môn
prov_r15_8_ruin_3.look: A ruined gate and halls on the grassland, with a stone sabre rack in the yard.
prov_r15_8_ruin_3.lore: A small sect of saber fighters founded in 560. Its head left on a journey in 870 and never returned, and the disciples scattered by 872.

prov_r15_9_peak_1.name: Ngư Ông Phong
prov_r15_9_peak_1.look: A peak on the cape shaped like a fisherman bent over his line.
prov_r15_9_peak_1.lore: Its qi runs to Water. Fishermen steer by it, and cultivators of Water arts sit on its spray-wet ledge at dawn.

prov_r15_9_mine_2.name: Thanh Thiết Khoáng
prov_r15_9_mine_2.look: Blue-grey iron ore in a mountain cut above the sea.
prov_r15_9_mine_2.lore: Its iron ore is carried down to boats and shipped to Tinh Hán's quays. Smiths say it takes a fine edge.
